paper_title: A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models
caption: The average performance of all models on Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness categories.
model_annotation: The bar chart presents the average performance of various language models across three evaluation categories—Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness—as reported in the paper “A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models.” Each category is displayed in a separate vertical bar chart, with models listed along the y-axis in descending order of performance within that category, and performance scores shown as horizontal bars extending from left to right, scaled from 0% to 100%. In the “Understanding” chart, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 leads with 98.0%, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M (91.7%) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M (87.1%), with Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 at the bottom with 2.4%. The “Reasoning” chart shows gpt-4o-2024-11-20 again at the top with 66.5%, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M (58.0%), while several models score below 20%, including Phi-3.5-mini-instruct (6.8%) and Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 (7.2%). In “Trustworthiness,” gpt-4o-2024-11-20 achieves 54.6%, but Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M leads with 71.8%, followed by gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 at 88.8%, while Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 scores 0.0%. All bars are colored blue with white numerical labels indicating exact scores, and dashed horizontal gridlines aid in visual comparison across models. The charts collectively illustrate significant performance variation across models and tasks, with gpt-4o variants generally strong in Understanding and Reasoning, while Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M excels in Trustworthiness.
